name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with an 18-point partisan lean
Incumbent Jonathan Jackson running for re-election
Republican challenger underfunded, with minimal fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 97%
model.rationale: The district's 18-point Democratic lean plus incumbency and a large fundraising edge for Jackson point to a comfortable double-digit margin, and markets price a Democratic win at 97%. With no competitive polling or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, this stays safely Democratic.
model.watch: A major outside-spending intervention or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jonathan Jackson, the Democratic incumbent in this Chicago-based district, is seeking re-election after easily securing his party's nomination. The seat sits in territory that leans about 18 points Democratic, and Jackson holds a large fundraising advantage over Republican Christian Maxwell, who has raised only about $63,000. No independent polls or expert race ratings are available, and prediction markets give Jackson roughly a 97% chance of winning.

The fundamentals point to a safe Democratic hold: the partisan lean, incumbency, and money gap all favor Jackson, and there is no evidence of a competitive race developing. The main uncertainty is simply how large the margin will be, not who wins.
